key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on jointly designing load transfer, surface architecture, and bone–implant integration rather than optimizing coatings or geometry alone.
engineering_relevance: Implant development should couple gait-informed mechanical design with fatigue-resistant, biologically compatible interfaces and coating-integrity testing.
method: Systematic review of implant geometry, biomaterials, and clinical translation.
Synthesis of gait-phase finite element modeling and graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces.
Quantitative trend analysis of evidence maturity and validation depth.
evidence_signal: The review analyzed 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies, with more than half of empirical evidence remaining at bench or simulation level.
watch_item: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite concepts rely predominantly on non-DWBI analog studies, so their promise should not be mistaken for device-specific validation.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
